probe.format_note: Single 9:16 film, 720x1280, 30 fps, 33.44 s (matches our default vertical format, no re-composition needed). Audio: AAC HE-AACv2 stereo 44.1 kHz, continuous (no silence below -40 dB for 0.3 s or longer), mean -16.9 dB, peak -0.5 dB; the on-screen caption changes phrase by phrase like a narrated script, so read as narration over a music bed (not listened to, not analysed for beats); third-party audio, never reused.

mode.why: third-party motivational reel of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and the glowing 2.5D shape look only, never its shots one by one, its copy or its scene order (owner note); the whole film is one glossy jelly glyph travelling through an abstract glowing world, the JOURNEY pattern; with a voiceover package L4 may still run it as a REEL arc drawn in this world

ignored.why: all English copy (the motivational script: 'when you feel stuck, or dissatisfied in your life, it's a signal ... most basic needs are not being met ... your need for exploration ... everything grows for your entire life, and your soul needs exploration & growth, and the only way you'll get it is by forcing yourself to be uncomfortable') is third-party copy; never reused, translated or paraphrased as our line

the specific metaphors tied to that script (a glass phone-like frame for 'stuck', the cup-like ring filling for 'needs', dunes with a tower for 'exploration', a cone growing for 'grows', a compass star for 'soul', a ledge and stepping pads for 'uncomfortable') are the creator's scene ideas; only the techniques may be used, on subjects taken from our voice-over
the audio track (narration and music) is third-party; L2 uses our voice-over and L6 builds our sound

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 at 480 px wide (6 sheets, 4x3, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found 3 cuts: 13.20, 18.37, 27.63 s; the rest of the film is one continuous morphing shot, so the other shot boundaries (about 2.0, 4.5, 7.5, 9.0, 15.5, 20.5, 23.9, 31.8 s) are motion beats found by eye on the 2 fps sheets; dense sheets at fps=10 around 12.7-13.9, 17.8-19.0, 23.3-24.5 and 27.1-28.3 s (4 dense sheets, all viewed). Spans accurate to about ±0.1 s at detected cuts and ±0.25 s at beats found by eye. silencedetect + volumedetect on the audio. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

shots.shot: medium, centred: a tall rounded-rectangle frame drawn as a glowing outline (white on one side fading to cyan on the other), with a glossy jelly ball resting at its bottom edge, on the near-black starfield
shots.camera: locked, the frame grows slightly from about 75% to 100% of its size over the first second (smooth ease-out)
shots.moves: 0-0.5 s the frame scales up from the centre; 0.3-1.6 s wide glossy diagonal light stripes (cyan to white gradient) slide through the inside of the frame from top to bottom, clipped by it; small glowing pills and squares fly in from outside the frame on arcs and hit its edges, sliding behind it; 1.5-2.0 s the stripes exit at the top and a pill streaks away off the bottom edge
shots.transition_out: no cut: the stripes clear and the empty frame stays for the next beat (2.0 s)
shots.palette: near-black navy ground, white-to-cyan glowing outline, cyan and electric-blue glossy stripes and pills, pale blue jelly ball with a white rim
shots.built: code-native (SVG or canvas: rounded-rect stroke with gradient, clip path for the stripes, bloom layer)
shots.reusable: yes: a container drawn as a glowing outline, filled for a moment by sliding light stripes and particles hitting its edges, to say 'boxed in' or 'full'; motion only, our subject from the voice-over

shots.shot: same frame, now empty and dark inside, the jelly ball alone at the bottom
shots.moves: 2.0-3.5 s the ball bounces inside the frame with squash and stretch (it stretches tall on the rise, squashes on the floor, smears into a double blob when it hits the left wall), elastic and springy; 3.4-4.4 s the outline erases itself: the stroke unwinds from the top-right corner around the frame like a line being undrawn (smooth, about 1 s), leaving the ball floating free
shots.transition_out: no cut: the outline is gone and the ball stays, moved up to the centre (4.5 s)
shots.built: code-native (SVG path with stroke-dashoffset for the undraw, ball as an SVG blob with squash and stretch)
shots.reusable: yes: a lone character bounces against the walls of a box, then the box undraws itself and frees it; motion only

shots.shot: medium, centred low: the glossy ball alone, then the source of a burst of wide light beams
shots.moves: 4.5 s a four-point star glint flashes on the ball's upper left (about 0.3 s); 5.0-5.4 s three wide wedge-shaped light beams shoot out from the ball to the frame edges (fast ease-out), with thin cyan spark rays radiating between them; 5.5-7.0 s the beams and rays rotate slowly around the ball; 7.0-7.5 s the beams sweep off-frame and fade, the ball alone again
shots.transition_out: no cut: the beams leave and the ball holds (7.5 s)
shots.palette: white-to-electric-blue beams with a cyan tip, white glint, cyan spark rays
shots.built: code-native (SVG wedges with linear gradients, rotating group, bloom)
shots.reusable: yes: a single glint then a burst of light beams from one point to mark the key word ('signal', 'idea', 'answer'); motion only

shots.shot: medium, centred high: the ball breaks into pieces
shots.moves: 7.8-8.3 s the ball splits into shards (two crescent halves, a small drop and a little square) that spring apart outward (snappy then elastic settle); 8.3-8.8 s the shards drift apart and fall away to the sides while an empty glowing outline ring is left where the ball was
shots.transition_out: no cut: the shards are gone, the empty ring holds (9.0 s)
shots.palette: cyan and pale blue glossy shards with white rims; white outline ring
shots.reusable: yes: a whole shape breaks into a few clean glossy pieces and leaves its empty outline behind, to show something missing or broken; motion only

shots.shot: medium: the empty outline ring high in the frame, a soft light column rising from the bottom edge
shots.camera: locked until 12.7 s, then the ring travels up and to the right out of frame
shots.moves: 9.0-9.6 s a glowing vertical light column grows up from the bottom edge behind the caption, with a horizontal band of blurred pixel-like bars across the bottom (light slides along it like a scanning bar); 9.5-11.0 s small particles (a white asterisk flower, cyan pills, tiny squares) orbit around the ring and fly through; 10.5-12.5 s liquid fills the bottom of the ring and sloshes side to side (smooth, wave-like); 12.6-13.1 s the ring rises and slides to the upper right, leaving the frame

shots.transition_out: hard cut (13.2 s) just as the ring exits upper right
shots.palette: white ring, cyan liquid, cyan-to-pale-blue light column, mixed cyan and steel-blue bars at the bottom

shots.reusable: yes: an empty container that only partly fills, its liquid sloshing low, to show a need not met; motion only

shots.shot: wide: two overlapping glossy hills fill the lower half (cyan crest fading to electric blue), a white glowing capsule tower stands on the back hill, starfield above
shots.moves: 13.2-13.6 s the jelly ball rolls in from the left edge along the front hill, squashing as it rolls (smooth); 13.4 s a star glint flashes on the tower top; 13.6-14.8 s hold while the ball settles; 14.8-15.5 s the front hill pours forward and morphs into a big capsule-shaped jelly outline that slides down out of frame (shape morph, smooth)

shots.shot: wide: a curved planet horizon fills the lower third (grainy white rim light along the curve, deep electric blue below), a glossy capsule resting on it

shots.palette: white grainy rim, electric blue to cyan planet, cyan-to-white light cone, white lens flare
shots.built: code-native (SVG arc with a grain texture, gradient cone, flare as thin crossed lines with bloom)
shots.reusable: yes: a beam of light grows from the ground and lifts the character, topped by a flare; then a match-on-action cut carries a moving element into the next scene; motion only

shots.shot: medium: one glowing jelly shape alone in the dark starfield
shots.moves: 18.37-19.3 s a long thin pill enters from the left and tumbles across the frame, getting shorter and fatter; 19.3-20.0 s it morphs from pill to bean to an oval (continuous shape morph, smooth, with slight elastic wobble); 20.0-20.5 s it becomes a round ball and drifts to the centre

shots.shot: medium to wide: the ball rides on the tip of a tall flaring cone that grows up from the bottom edge like a fountain or tent
shots.camera: rising: the world slides down past the camera, shown by thin vertical speed lines falling and big lens-blurred glossy bubbles passing in the foreground

shots.transition_out: the shape thins to a point, then a near-cut to a dot at the centre of the next shot (about 23.9 s, not caught by scene detect)
shots.palette: cyan to white to electric-blue cone, glossy blue bubbles out of focus, pale speed lines

visual_language: An abstract glowing-shape explainer reel: one glossy jelly ball is the protagonist of the whole film and travels through a sequence of simple luminous metaphors (a box, a burst, broken pieces, an empty cup, hills, a planet, a rising cone, a bright disc, a ledge and steps), one per narration phrase, all on the same near-black starfield. Medium: code-built 2.5D vector shapes with gradient fills, bloom and glossy highlights. Typography: only one small caption line (light rounded monospace-like grotesk, lowercase, white with a soft glow, cap height about 1.2% of frame height, centred at about 82% of height) that changes phrase by phrase with the narration; no hero type at all, the shapes carry the meaning. Rhythm: only 3 real cuts in 33 s; between them the film is one continuous morph where each shape becomes the next, with a new motion beat every 1.5-3 s on the caption phrase; average beat about 2.8 s. Easing: elastic squash and stretch on the jelly, fast ease-out pops and bursts, smooth slow drifts and morphs. Palette: near-black navy ground, electric blue, cyan and white light, nothing else. Signature moments: stripes of light sliding through a glass frame; the frame undrawing itself to free the ball; a light-beam burst from the ball; the ball shattering into crescents and leaving an empty ring; liquid sloshing low in the ring; rolling onto glowing hills; a light cone growing from a planet and a match-on-action cut; a pill morphing into a ball; the ball riding a rising cone with speed lines; a dot opening into a bright disc wrapped by neon ribbons; a squash-and-stretch leap to a floating pad.
look: Flat-to-2.5D glowing vector, not real 3D: shapes are flat paths with smooth linear gradients (cyan to electric blue to white), each with a strong soft bloom halo. Light and shadow: no cast shadows; light comes from the shapes themselves (glows, beams, lens-flare stars, grainy rim light on the planet edge). Materials: glossy jelly (translucent blue body, bright white rim, specular highlight on the upper left), glowing neon tubes, emissive outlines. Depth: almost none, faked twice by lens-blurred foreground bubbles and by pads shrinking toward the top; no perspective. Background: deep near-black navy with sparse tiny star specks and a faint soft vignette glow, constant through the whole film.
code_translation: Built in 2D code, which is faithful because the reference itself is 2.5D (not a 3D film flattened): SVG or canvas shapes with linear and radial gradients mapped onto brand colour roles (ground, accent, secondary accent, highlight); bloom as stacked blurred copies or a canvas glow pass; jelly characters as SVG blobs with squash-and-stretch transforms and path morphing between forms (ball, pill, bean, capsule, shards) with a spring ease; outlines drawn and undrawn with stroke-dashoffset; beams and cones as gradient wedges; lens-flare stars as thin crossed lines with glow; foreground depth as CSS blur on large shapes; speed lines as falling strokes. Caption: one centred line in the brand Persian font, whole words only, never split letters (rtl-grammar.md), larger than the reference to meet the minimum size; centred so it mirrors cleanly for Persian. Subjects come from our voice-over, never the reference's.
continuity: One protagonist glyph: a single glossy jelly ball is present in almost every shot and carries the eye from metaphor to metaphor.
One world: the same near-black starfield and glow light in every shot, so the three cuts feel like moves inside one place.
Shape becomes shape: instead of cutting, one form morphs into the next (frame to empty frame, ball to shards to ring, hill to capsule to horizon, pill to bean to ball).
Undraw to free: a container's outline unwinds itself like a line being erased, leaving only what was inside.
Break and leave the outline: a solid shape splits into a few pieces that fly off, and its empty outline stays as the next subject.
Exit with momentum: an element leaves the frame on a clear path and the cut lands as it exits.
Match on action: a moving element leaves one shot and enters the next from the opposite edge, still moving the same way.
Collapse to a point, open from a point: a shape thins down to a single dot and the next scene grows out of a dot at the centre.
Constant caption line: one small phrase line at the same height in every shot changes with the narration while the shapes carry the meaning.
Squash and stretch as emotion: the jelly character bounces, gathers and leaps, so effort and freedom read through its body.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its English script, its metaphors as a set, its scene order one by one, or its audio.

The caption line is tiny (cap height about 1.2% of frame height, about 15 px at 1280) and set low at about 82% of height: in our film it must meet the minimum text size, hold times and the bottom safe zone (safe-zones.md), so it is set larger and placed inside the safe zone.

Persian runs right to left: the centred caption mirrors cleanly, but the ball rolling in from the left, the match-on-action move left to right and the leap to the right are mirrored for Persian (rtl-grammar.md).
The film has no hero type: key words and numbers in our package still need on-screen text; add them as a short line or a single word in the brand font inside this glow world, not a new style.
The look is 2.5D glow vector, so a 2D build (SVG or canvas with bloom) is faithful; three.js is not needed, but bloom and blur layers add render time.
The palette is near-black navy, electric blue, cyan and white: mapped onto brand colour roles, never the literal cyan if the brand bans it; colours read by eye, not sampled.
Only 3 cuts were detected; the other shot boundaries are motion beats found by eye (±0.25 s); our film's beats are placed on voice timing, not on these spans.
A dark background with strong glow can band or block up after compression: keep gradients smooth and add slight grain, and check contrast of the caption over bright beams and cones.
Audio is third-party narration and music; ignored, L2 and L6 build ours.
